import numpy as np
from scipy import stats
from sklearn.feature_selection import mutual_info_classif
from sklearn.preprocessing import StandardScaler

MAX_DRIVERS = 4

def design(feats):
    # Filter out near-duplicates based on correlation
    ids = list(feats.ids)
    types = list(feats.types)
    x = feats.x
    y = feats.y
    
    # Build correlation matrix
    corr_matrix = np.corrcoef(x.T)
    to_remove = set()
    for i in range(len(ids)):
        for j in range(i+1, len(ids)):
            if abs(corr_matrix[i,j]) >= 0.6:
                to_remove.add(j)
    
    # Keep only unique features
    keep = [i for i in range(len(ids)) if i not in to_remove]
    ids_keep = [ids[i] for i in keep]
    x_keep = x[:, keep]
    
    # Compute effect sizes (mean difference in outcome groups)
    means_0 = np.mean(x_keep[y==0], axis=0)
    means_1 = np.mean(x_keep[y==1], axis=0)
    effect_sizes = np.abs(means_1 - means_0)
    
    # Sort by effect size
    sorted_idx = np.argsort(effect_sizes)[::-1]
    
    # Select top features as potential drivers
    drivers = []
    columns = []
    products = []
    loadings = {}
    
    # Take top 4 features as drivers (or fewer if less available)
    num_drivers = min(MAX_DRIVERS, len(sorted_idx))
    for i in range(num_drivers):
        fid = ids_keep[sorted_idx[i]]
        drivers.append(fid)
        columns.append(fid)
        loadings[fid] = effect_sizes[sorted_idx[i]]
        
    # Add interaction terms between top two drivers if they exist
    if len(drivers) >= 2:
        a, b = drivers[0], drivers[1]
        products.append((a,b))
        columns.append(a)
        columns.append(b)
        
    # Remove duplicates from columns
    columns = list(set(columns))
    
    return Design(
        drivers=tuple(drivers),
        columns=tuple(columns),
        products=tuple(products),
        loadings=loadings
    )
